answer: No, your dad doesn't need a notary in Virginia. He can sign the current power of attorney form, NW-POA-2, electronically. It replaced the older notarized form NW-POA-1 on February 1, 2026, and the NW-POA-1 is no longer accepted after June 30, 2026. Only Georgia still requires a power of attorney to be notarized. Bring the signed form, your own photo ID and the car's documents to the appointment, and keep in mind that a power of attorney ends if the person who signed it dies.
